comments.body: This looks amazing. Will look at it in a few days. I've been in over my head with stuff these last few days.

@zsviczian Thank you for testing this and for the detailed feedback. I've opened a fresh two-file replacement in **#2925** and am closing this older PR as superseded.

The replacement still adds only `ea-scripts/LayerManager.md` and `ea-scripts/LayerManager.svg`; the icon is unchanged. Changes since this PR:

- Same-leaf Excalidraw → Markdown → Excalidraw recovery no longer needs a script rerun, including delayed scene-API readiness.
- Closing the manager cleans up its owned listeners/subscriptions/timers, and pending startup/mutation work cannot revive a disposed invocation. Reruns coordinate shared-tab ownership.
- Ordinary element labels are now written only to `customData.lmx.label`; native `name` is used for frames. Existing legacy fields and unrelated metadata are preserved rather than bulk-migrated.
- Native EA staging is isolated per mutation, preventing old staged elements from overwriting unrelated canvas edits while preserving native undo/redo.
- Rectangle/frame rename drafts retain focus and caret through refresh. Stale detached-input events cannot commit/cancel the current editor; Enter/blur commit once and Escape cancels.

Source-project CI passes **753 tests / 67 files**. The exact outgoing script was also reinstalled and dogfooded in an isolated Linux vault on **Obsidian 1.13.7 / Excalidraw 2.27.3**, including recovery, inline editing, stale events, staging preservation, undo/redo and save/reopen. This is scoped verification, not a claim of exhaustive memory-leak freedom or all-platform coverage.

Thumbnails and presenter/shared-metadata interoperability remain outside this corrective revision. Your original testing feedback stays linked from #2925. Please review the replacement there when you have time—thanks again!
